items.title: RBI appoints Smt. Monisha Chakraborty as new Executive Director
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has appointed Smt. Monisha Chakraborty as Executive Director (ED) with effect from August 3, 2026. Prior to being promoted as ED, Smt. Monisha Chakraborty was serving as Chief General Manager -in- Charge in Department of Supervision. As a career central banker, Smt. Monisha Chakraborty has experience of over three decades in the Reserve Bank, having worked in the areas of Supervision, Foreign Exchange and Government and Bank Accounts. She was associated with a technical Committee set up to review the format of the RBI’s Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss account.

items.title: $100 bn in sight: India is rolling in dollars but what about the rupee?
items.summary: Two months after the RBI launched special measures to attract foreign currency, banks have mobilised over $40 billion, led by FCNR(B) deposits, with economists projecting inflows could reach $100 billion. The programme is aimed at strengthening India's external defences and ensuring dollar liquidity during global volatility, rather than boosting the rupee, which has remained largely unchanged.

items.title: Blackstone-backed Aadhar Housing sees no need to raise capital for four years; bets on smaller towns to sustain growth
items.summary: Rishi Anand, MD & CEO, said the lender's increasing presence in talukas and district centres is expected to strengthen growth without compromising asset quality.

items.title: India, Uzbekistan could explore FTA, says Piyush Goyal; Uzbekistan invites Indian investment in mining, rare earths
items.summary: India and Uzbekistan aim to double bilateral trade to three billion dollars within three years. Businesses are urged to increase investments and explore opportunities in key sectors. India offers strengths in information technology and a skilled workforce for collaboration. Uzbekistan presents opportunities in mining and cotton production for mutual benefit. Both nations are considering a potential free trade agreement to boost economic ties.

items.title: New Tax Bill sweetens deal for electronics makers, global investors
items.summary: The Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill, 2026 proposes extending electronics tax incentives until 2041, easing rules for foreign investors and fund managers, while raising surcharge on certain SPVs under the new tax regime.

items.title: US and Japan take action to prop up yen in rare joint move
items.summary: Both countries have said that they will not hesitate to conduct joint interventions in the future.

items.title: Swiggy, Eternal chart different paths to expand India’s food delivery market
items.summary: Swiggy is banking on affordability through its dedicated meals app Toing to attract price-sensitive consumers, using its existing restaurant and delivery ecosystem. Eternal is investing in Bistro, redesigning kitchen operations and supply chains to prepare low-priced meals.

items.title: Della bets on 3,600-key hotel pipeline to drive township projects
items.summary: Della is betting that destination attractions such as adventure sports, wellness, motorsports and weddings can generate year-round footfall, boosting both hotel occupancy and the value of surrounding real estate.

items.title: India's manufacturing activity slips to near five-year low in July but signals solid growth
items.summary: A sharp moderation in new orders curbed input purchasing, even as export demand strengthened and inflationary pressures moderated, showed HSBC India Manufacturing PMI

items.title: IndiGo appoints former IATA chief Willie Walsh as CEO to lead airline's global expansion
items.summary: IndiGo has officially appointed former IATA chief Willie Walsh as its new Chief Executive Officer. The aviation veteran will lead the airline's global expansion, international network growth and long-term strategy.

items.title: Team America: Yen police
items.summary: A puzzling intervention

items.title: India's July factory growth near five-year low on weaker demand, PMI shows
items.summary: India's manufacturing growth slowed to a near five-year low in July as weak demand weighed on new orders, while hiring growth softened for a third month. Easing input cost inflation offered some relief and business confidence improved slightly.

items.title: Bharti Airtel Q1 may see steady growth, flat Arpu
items.summary: Bharti Airtel's net profit is expected to increase 47% on-year and 20% on-quarter to ₹8,759 crore in Q1FY27.

items.title: Beefing with the Big Mac Index
items.summary: McDonald’s signature burger offers economic lessons — but not about purchasing power parity

items.title: Is AI eating away IT jobs? Zoho's Sridhar Vembu blames ‘steep rise in server and memory prices’ for lack of jobs
items.summary: Zoho's Sridhar Vembu sparked debate on impact of AI disruption on India's IT industry. Suggesting that AI is eating away IT jobs, he blamed ‘steep rise in server and memory prices’ for lack of jobs.

items.title: Will a repo rate pause make RBI fall behind the curve?
items.summary: Facing rising inflation risks from the West Asia war and El Niño, the RBI faces dilemma over whether to hold repo rates or hike them to curb mounting price pressures.

items.title: New Spider-Man film sees second-biggest ever global opening weekend
items.summary: The strong box office performance gives a boost to Disney ahead of the much-anticipated Avengers: Doomsday.

items.summary: The ‘junk’ label has been left where it belongs — in a different era

items.title: Whatever happened to prudence?
items.summary: Governments have stopped correcting budget deficits but — so far — bond markets have let them

items.title: Wall Street learns to love blockchain
items.summary: Financial companies hope to modernise markets with the technology but systemic risks remain

items.title: RBI MPC begins today as policymakers weigh inflation, crude risks
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee begins its meeting this week. Market participants widely expect the benchmark repo rate to remain unchanged. Experts believe the central bank will focus on domestic inflation and growth. Global uncertainties and elevated crude oil prices are closely monitored. Future policy decisions will consider these evolving domestic and external factors.

items.title: September’s blockbuster NSE, Jio listings to add to IPO rebound
items.summary: Mega IPOs from NSE and Jio Platforms are expected to revive India’s primary market, boosting investor sentiment and unlocking a packed pipeline of companies waiting to go public.

items.title: How Satyaki Ghosh plans to restore Raymond Lifestyle to its former glory
items.summary: Ghosh, who took the reins at Raymond Lifestyle in January, has earmarked FY27 as a year of consolidation, closing loss-making stores, streamlining operations and doubling down on premiumisation and casualisation before embarking on the company’s next phase of growth.

items.title: Instant-help apps want to expand, but economics don't add up
items.summary: Experts say Snabbit, Pronto and InstaHelp may need to raise prices to well above ₹200 an hour to make the instant-help model profitable beyond high-density neighbourhoods.

items.title: RBI set to hold rates on 5 Aug as global risks cloud outlook: Mint poll
items.summary: Economists expect the RBI to keep the repo rate and policy stance unchanged, with markets watching its guidance on inflation, growth, the rupee and the timing of any future rate moves.

items.title: AI disruption hits Wipro as Meta trims outsourcing engagement
items.summary: In FY26, Wipro generated about $100 million in annual revenue from Meta, which is among the IT services company’s 20 largest accounts. Wipro is now expected to generate about $75 million in annual revenue from Meta after the social media company ended outsourcing for its digital marketing work.

items.title: Global insurers look to tap India opportunity as 100% FDI lures
items.summary: India's insurance market is becoming a magnet for global insurers, with South Korea's Hanwha Group and South Africa's Discovery among those evaluating opportunities after India allowed 100% foreign ownership. This is set to spur acquisitions and deepen competition across the under-penetrated sector.

items.title: Fewer jobs in the market? Some of India's top companies are hiring less
items.summary: Among the 30 Sensex companies, total new hires at nine companies fell 27% in FY26 compared to FY24 while two companies hired more, a Mint analysis found. The remaining companies either do not disclose or only partially disclose fresh hiring numbers.

items.title: Toyota expected to post fifth straight profit drop, investors weigh Japan quake fallout
items.summary: TOYOTA-RESULTS/ (PREVIEW, PIX):PREVIEW-Toyota expected to post fifth straight profit drop, investors weigh Japan quake fallout

items.title: Prysmian Is Said Near Takeover of US Electrical Maker Atkore
items.summary: Italy’s Prysmian is in advanced talks to acquire electrical manufacturing company Atkore Inc., people familiar with the matter said.

items.title: Data centres draw 40% of institutional capital in the June quarter
items.summary: Data centres are now the second-largest investment recipient, attracting substantial institutional capital. Rapid AI adoption and cloud expansion fuel investor interest in digital infrastructure assets. India's data centre capacity is projected to more than double by 2025. The current investment pipeline for data centres stands at approximately ninety billion dollars.

items.title: RBI special windows seen big enough to bring in $100B
items.summary: India's new forex inflow programs may attract approximately one hundred billion dollars. These special drives have already mobilized over forty billion dollars in foreign exchange. Experts predict these initiatives could significantly exceed initial mobilization estimates. The Reserve Bank of India introduced these facilities to support the balance of payments. These programs aim to cushion the rupee and contain imported inflation.

items.title: India, Canada aim to conclude CEPA trade pact by end-2026: MEA
items.summary: India and Canada are working to finalize their economic partnership agreement. Negotiations for the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement are progressing well. Both nations aim to conclude these important talks by the end of 2026. This agreement seeks to liberalize trade and strengthen economic cooperation between the two countries. Prime Minister Modi plans a visit later this year to boost bilateral ties.

items.title: Govt's urban reset: Centre divides ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs into two specialised verticals
items.summary: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has undergone a significant structural overhaul. Senior bureaucrats were replaced and new leadership appointed to spearhead its flagship missions. The ministry was split into two specialized departments, focusing on capital development and urban development. This administrative revamp aims to streamline service delivery and accelerate infrastructure projects. Personnel shifts occurred rapidly after the government's decision to divide the ministry.

items.title: Government plans to ease forex rule for SEZ services exports to domestic tariff areas
items.summary: The current provision under Section 2(z) of the SEZ Act, 2005 mandates that proceeds for SEZ to DTA supplies of services must be realised in foreign exchange, although there is no such requirement in case of supply of goods to DTA entities.

items.title: Processed food exports gain steam, US leads the rise in global appetite
items.summary: Exports of ready-to-eat and cooked food items increased 16% to $2.4 billion in 2025-26 from $2.1 billion in the previous financial year, according to an ET analysis. The analysis is based on 11 items including pasta, sweet biscuits, pastries, papad, coffee and tea.

items.title: America’s biggest companies report ‘rock solid’ profits as consumers face higher costs
items.summary: S&P 500 groups on track for strongest earnings in five years

items.title: Government aims to complete Mumbai's Coastal Road project by Dec 2028: Union Minister Piyush Goyal
items.summary: The Bandra-Versova-Bhayander Coastal Road project aims for completion by December 2028. This infrastructure development will significantly reduce travel times across Mumbai's western suburbs. Additional projects, including a desalination plant, are also under review for future implementation.

items.title: India clears only one Chinese FDI proposal worth Rs 1 crore in FY26; approves 13 Hong Kong investments
items.summary: India approved one Chinese FDI proposal worth Rs 1 crore during FY26. Thirteen proposals from Hong Kong totaling Rs 610.42 crore received government clearance. Overall, sixty-three FDI proposals worth Rs 10,292.67 crore were approved by the government. Singapore and the UK emerged as top FDI sources by value. These figures align with previous financial year trends for Chinese investments.

items.title: Walter insurers paid millions of dollars to credit rating provider Egan-Jones
items.summary: Billionaire investor faces wide-ranging probe into the private credit holdings of insurers he controls

items.title: Will July’s US employment data prompt a rethink on rates?
items.summary: Market Questions is the FT’s guide to the week ahead

items.title: NBA releases Rs 8.22 crore to rice research institutions and rice-growing States
items.summary: Of the total amount, Rs 2.47 crore has been released to research institutions that conserved and shared the rice varieties with the company. ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad, has received the largest share of Rs 2.43 crore, while Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Uttarakhand, has received Rs 3.26 lakh for the specific rice variety it contributed, the release said.

items.title: Morgan Stanley’s IPO after-party: a wealth management bonanza
items.summary: Bank’s underwriting of SpaceX and other new issues generates $74bn second-quarter haul in wealth management assets

items.title: Beyond El Niño: The bigger risks facing Indian agriculture
items.summary: After a listless June, agricultural sowing picked up well in July, though it's still lower than last year. The cloud of El Niño apart, Indian agriculture also has to deal with the debilitating effects of other structural problems.

items.title: An exam leak in India exposed a Gen Z jobs crisis that goes much deeper
items.summary: While the leak of key exam papers was the trigger for the recent student protest in India, rising unemployment is the real fuel angering Gen Z in the country.
